name: Vivek Chand Burman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025)
forbes_bio: Chairman emeritus of Indian consumer goods outfit Dabur, Vivek Chand Burman, is the oldest member of the founding Burman clan.
Dabur was started by his great-grandfather in 1884 to sell ayurvedic medicines.
He joined the company in 1954 and became chairman in 1998 holding that post for close to a decade.
In 2007, he handed over charge to nephew Anand Burman, who is also a billionaire. His son, Mohit, was appointed chairman of Dabur in 2022.
Burman has a stake in Kolkata-based battery maker Eveready Industries.
forbes_facts: Burman's sons Mohit and Gaurav are involved in a slew of privately-held ventures ranging from sports and healthcare to financial services and real estate.
Gaurav owns the franchise for Taco Bell in India.

name: Casey Foyt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Foyt is the granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who acquired the Indianapolis Colts in 1972, and the middle daughter of Jim Irsay, who ran the team from 1997 until his death in May 2025.
She and her sisters, Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Kalen Jackson, inherited what Forbes estimates are equal 33.3% stakes in the franchise. They now rank among the richest female owners in sports.

Long before the three sisters were publicly named Colts co-owners in 2012, their lives revolved around the NFL schedule. At an introductory press conference in June 2025, Foyt recalled answering the phones at the front desk while she was in high school.
Early in her career, Foyt worked for the NFL, where she helped plan the league's first regular-season game played outside North America, in London in 2007.
She returned to the Colts that year with a focus on marketing and community relationships.

name: Alessandro Rosano
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025)
forbes_bio: Alessandro Rosano is the founder of HeyDude, a line of comfort shoes.
He and his business partner and U.S. distributor, Daniele Guidi, sold the business to Crocs for $2.5 billion in 2022.

Before starting HeyDude, Rosano had launched a number of businesses, including a wooden watch brand called WeWood and a line of wooden clogs with springs in their heels that sold under the name Baldo.
He grew up in Pistoia, Italy, a medieval city not far from Florence, and moved to Hong Kong to run his businesses.
With comfort shoes having a moment, HeyDude sales soared from $20 million in 2018 to $581 million in 2021, when Crocs agreed to buy the brand. Revenue for the latest 12 months is now over $1 billion.
forbes_facts: Rosano built the HeyDude brand with no investment and minimal marketing.

name: Liu Jingkang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026)
forbes_bio: Liu Jingkang founded camera maker Arashi Vision, also known as Insta360, in 2015.
The company's products include handheld 360-degree cameras capable of taking spherical videos in high-resolution quality.
Headquartered in Shenzhen, China, Insta360 has opened offices in the U.S., Japan and Germany.
Its backers include Qiming Venture Partners, IDG Capital Partners and Chinese retailer Suning Group.
The company went public on the Shanghai stock exchange in June 2025.

name: Frank McCourt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Frank McCourt is an investor and entrepreneur with roots in his family's Boston-based construction business founded five generations ago.
In 2004, McCourt bought the Los Angeles Dodgers and sold the team for $2.2 billion eight years later, the largest sports sale at the time.
McCourt invested the proceeds into real estate, sports, tech and media through his company McCourt Global.
He stepped down as CEO of McCourt Global in 2023 to focus on Project Liberty, his $500 million commitment to fight for a safe, healthier internet.
McCourt has also pledged $200 million to his alma mater, Georgetown, helping establish the McCourt School of Public Policy.

name: Hans Thomann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Hans Thomann is managing director of Thomann, one of Europe's largest music retailers with locations in Germany, France and Denmark, among others.
Thomann took over the business from his father, who started the company in 1954, and expanded it during the dot-com-era of the 1990s and 2000s.
Today Thommann employs more than 1,800 people who come from 55 countries.
The company is still headquartered in the small German town of Treppendorf.
The sole owner of the company, Thomann became involved in the business when he was 12 years of age.

name: Michael Cagney
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2025)
forbes_bio: Mike Cagney is cofounder of blockchain technology company Figure Technology Solutions.
Cagney cofounded Figure with his wife June Ou in 2018 and took the company public on the Nasdaq in September 2025.
Cagney served as CEO of Figure until 2024, while Ou served as chief operating officer until 2022. Both still sit on the company's board.
Before Figure, Cagney cofounded fintech company SoFi in 2011 and ran it as chairman and CEO until 2017. Ou served as SoFi's chief technology officer from 2012 to 2017.
Cagney started his career at Wells Fargo and went on to found wealth management software company Finaplex and hedge fund Cabezon Investment Group.

name: Peng Hao

forbes_bio: Peng Hao chairs Shenzhen Sunway Communication, a maker of telecommunication parts.
Sunway listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.
Peng founded Sunway in his dorm in Shajin Changxing Industrial Park in Shenzhen.

name: Koon Poh Ming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Koon Poh Ming is the executive vice chairman of aluminum company Press Metal while his brother Koon Poh Keong is group CEO.
They started Press Metal with their three brothers--Poh Tat, Poh Weng and Poh Kong--in the mid-1980s.
The brothers pooled $50,000 to start the aluminum-extruding company, at a time when Malaysia was in a recession.
Press Metal is Southeast Asia's largest integrated aluminum producer and competes with Rio Tinto, Russia's RUSAL and the Aluminum Corp of China.
Poh Ming and Poh Keong, the two biggest shareholders, made the list of Malaysia's richest for the first time in 2017. Poh Weng joined them in 2019.
forbes_facts: Poh Ming launched the company with his brothers by renting a factory in Puchong, Selangor, on the west coast of peninsular Malaysia.

name: Mao Zhongwu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Mao Zhongwu is a founder of the Sany Group, a construction equipment manufacturer.
Mao is one of three billionaires from Sany Group including Liang Wengen and Xiang Wenbo.
Mao resigned as a director at Sany International in October 2019.

name: Ruben Feffer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Ruben Feffer is one of four billionaire brothers who control Suzano, a Brazilian paper giant founded by their grandfather.
He has developed a career creating music for movies and TV shows.
Ruben, a pianist, is credited with the music for Boy and the World, a 2013 Brazilian film nominated for Academy Award for best animated feature.
Known as Binho, he is not a board member at Suzano.
forbes_facts: Feffer is the founder of the production studio Ultrassom Music Ideas.
He has served as the musical director for a number of animated children's TV shows in Brazil.

name: Cheah Cheng Hye
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Cheah Cheng Hye is honorary chairman of Hong Kong-listed asset management firm Value Partners Group, which he cofounded in 1993 and took public in 2007.
He stepped down as cochairman in January 2025.
Born in Malaysia, he worked as a reporter, subeditor and writer at the Star newspaper in the country after leaving Penang Free School with a high school diploma.
In 1974, he traveled to Hong Kong, where he had stints in journalism at the Standard, HK-TVB News, the Asian Wall Street Journal and the Far Eastern Economic Review.
He worked at Morgan Grenfell Group in Hong Kong before starting Value Partners.
